source.title: Cross-Modal Unlearning via Influential Neuron Path Editing in Multimodal Large Language Models
source.authors: Kun-Hao Li; Wen-Hao Li; Di Wu; Lei Yang; Jun Bai; Ju Jia; Jason Xue

record.tranche_reason: Tests unlearning accuracy and retain-set performance with a different method in multimodal models, but does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates direct unlearning and utility before any recovery attack. It does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery. The results below bear on the unlearning-and-retention portion of version A only; cited work is not treated as this paper's result.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It proposes MIP-Editor, a neuron-path editing unlearning method for multimodal LLMs, and reports only its pre-attack forget and retain scores against baselines (GA Diff, KL Min, NPO, MANU). It runs no relearning, activation-ablation, quantization or prompting attack. The part of version A at issue in this phenomenon is that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge, so the study's results cannot show whether its unlearning is shallow. It also does not claim attack resistance, so it is not a version F test. All rows report the study's own method compared with others.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that MIP-Editor achieves effective, modality-consistent unlearning while preserving general utility, outperforming GA Diff, KL Min, NPO and MANU. They make no claim about robustness to recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: MIP-Editor locates modality-specific influential neuron paths, prunes path activations, and edits them using representation misdirection; the paper does not reproduce the original recovery-attack methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across backbone and dataset. The paper evaluates several forget ratios; it also reports that CLEAR results can be unstable under small learning-rate or batch-size adjustments.

fits_no_version.finding: An MLP classifier on post-unlearning logits separates forget-set from retain-set inputs at above 85% accuracy for MIP-Editor and near 50% for baselines on MLLMU-Bench (Fig. 7). Activation residuals are larger on forget inputs (Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Path-based unlearning leaves forget inputs distinguishable in output logits or activations, a separability measure rather than knowledge recovery.

record.problems: No recovery attacks are performed, so the paper provides no direct evidence about whether unlearned knowledge can be recovered. No error bars or other uncertainty estimates are stated. The authors note instability on CLEAR. The study uses two MLLMs and benchmark forget/retain splits.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 also reports comparator methods and generation metrics; Table 2 reports ablations; Table A2 reports additional forget ratios and CLEAR settings. These are not extracted here because they are pre-attack unlearning/utility results rather than recovery tests, and the rows retained capture the main accuracy-based results for the tested portion of A.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the forgotten knowledge. Only pre-attack forget and retain accuracy are reported.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation or access-versus-deletion recovery analysis. Activation residual heatmaps compare against the vanilla model only.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery test.
MIP-Editor is not evaluated against, and makes no claim about, any recovery attack.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' classification and its version-A labels are overturned. Reductions in pre-attack forget accuracy for a new method say nothing about whether unlearning is shallow. Forget accuracies as low as 0–5% on a QA benchmark may be well below chance, which could indicate steered wrong answers rather than deletion, but the study does not examine this. The CLEAR results are flagged by the authors as unstable.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning; the paper reports pre-attack forget-set and retain-set performance only.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning recovery attack.
No ablation of an activation direction to restore knowledge, and no test of access-blocking versus deletion as a recovery claim.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test.
MIP-Editor is evaluated for unlearning and utility, not for resistance to the attacks in the claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Forget-set accuracy falls substantially while RVQA retention is higher than Vanilla; this supports only the pre-attack unlearning/utility component, not attack resistance (R1-R3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: FVQA falls and RVQA exceeds Vanilla, supporting the pre-attack component in this setting; no recovery attack is tested (R11-R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
